member.name: DescendingSilenceScan
member.para: Where a book's chapter-bearing pauses actually rank (2026-08-19, replayed over the frozen build-341 logs in reference-marks/logs/). Sort a book's stored probe candidates by pause length, longest first, and find the deepest rank a chapter's own anchoring pause sits at. Over the eight pause-announced books of the seventeen: Rendezvous With Rama rank 45 of 514 (8.8 %), I Shall Wear Midnight 18 of 330 (5.5 %), Wintersmith 23 of 310 (7.4 %), The Forever War 98 of 686 (14.3 %), The Philosopher's Stone 51 of 223 (22.9 %), Corsa nello spazio 68 of 180 (37.8 %), Paula Monti 19 of 19, De vandrande djaeknarne 77 of 82. The precision at the top of the ranking is what makes the shape worth having: 65 of Corsa's top 68 candidates are chapters, and The Philosopher's Stone's top 14 are 14 chapters with nothing interleaved.

Seven of eight books have their first chapter anchor at rank 1 to 6 - the longest pause in a book is essentially always a chapter break. That is what makes dead weight on any book this shape can help, and therefore what makes deriving it better than calibrating it.

Total probes against the plain sweep's candidate count, simulated as "read down to the stop rule, then walk the file passing over what consecutive readings closed": Rama 15 %, I Shall Wear Midnight 33 %, The Forever War 35 %, The Philosopher's Stone 41 %, Corsa 43 %, Wintersmith 67 %, and Paula Monti and De vandrande djaeknarne 100 %. The last two are the shape's own worst case and they are exactly the plain sweep's cost, not double it, because a window read by the descent is not decoded again when the walk reaches it. What remains on such a book is decode locality rather than probe count - today's Probe serves 27 % to 55 % of its window seconds from the overlap cache (De vandrande djaeknarne 4 %), and a read that jumps around the file forfeits most of that.

What the saving really comes from, which was nearly mis-modelled: the file-order gate is a running minimum over the anchors of accepted marks, and on five of the six pause-announced corpus books it ends up at its 0.8 s floor and probes very nearly the whole candidate list - Rama 428 probes for 514 candidates, I Shall Wear Midnight 220 for 330, Wintersmith 356 for 310. It is that collapse the descending stop rule avoids, not some margin above the gate.

Paula Monti is the book with nothing to sort: 19 stored pauses in 4.6 hours, 19 of its 25 marks sitting on them. Nothing was added to the gate for it (the user's call, 2026-08-19, "keep it simple") - the shape reads all 19 longest-first and the second half adds six, which costs the cache and nothing else.

Not yet measured on the corpus. The replay above says where chapter pauses rank in a ranking; it does not say what a window framed by a different neighbour turns out to read, and the second half plans its windows inside a stretch rather than across the file. The next corpus run is the real test, and the blast-radius grep in the VAD-drift note bounds what can move on the placement side but not what a differently framed window may say.
